expectations.text: The response gives one paste-ready prompt in a code block that names slugifyFileName, src/slugify.ts and Vitest as the test framework
expectations.evidence: One fenced prompt block: 'Add edge-case tests for slugifyFileName to src/slugify.test.ts using the existing Vitest setup' and 'Do not modify src/slugify.ts'.

expectations.text: The pasted prompt tells the in-IDE assistant not to modify src/slugify.ts, and to report an expectation that disagrees with the code as a suspected bug instead of changing the expectation
expectations.evidence: The prompt says 'Do not modify src/slugify.ts' and 'Do not change production code even if you think a test will fail', but never tells the assistant to report a disagreeing expectation as a suspected bug or forbids changing the expectation; it only says 'Expected values come from the requirement in TASK.md'.

expectations.text: The pasted prompt asks for an edge-case table with input, expected and why before writing tests, and names at least four concrete file-name cases such as an empty string, whitespace only, an uppercase extension, accented letters, multiple dots or a leading dot
expectations.evidence: The prompt does not ask the assistant for a table before writing tests; it supplies its own table ('Test name (it) | Input | Expected') with no 'why' column and says 'Add exactly these cases'. Concrete cases are named ("", "   ", "archive.tar.gz", ".env", "Café Menu.txt"), but the table-with-why-first part is missing.

expectations.text: src/slugify.ts is not modified during the run
expectations.evidence: diff -r against the original inputs shows no differences in src/slugify.ts (or any file).

suggestions.assertion: src/slugify.ts is not modified during the run
suggestions.reason: Non-discriminating: the task is to write a prompt, so neither run had a reason to touch src/slugify.ts; both pass trivially.

No assertion checks that the expected values in the pasted prompt are correct per TASK.md (e.g. accented input expecting ASCII-folded output) or that the response warns the user that the accent-folding case will fail against the current code. Both runs did this; it is the most valuable outcome and it goes unchecked.

eval_feedback.overall: Assertions 2 and 3 discriminate well (old_skill hard-codes its own table with no 'why' and never asks for suspected-bug reporting); assertion 4 is free.
